EXERCISE 5a-5b   Complete the text with words from Ex 4, then listen and check.

A Police Detective's Job - The Basics

After a crime, the first thing detectives need to do is (a) investigate the case. Firstly, they (b) search for evidence, i.e. anything that can help to show that somebody in particular did the crime.

When they find the evidence, they need to (c) analyse it, studying it in detail. In that case, the police need to question the (d) witness.

When the police have specific evidence, they can (e) prove that the suspect committed the crime. When that happens, they can (f) accuse the suspect and say they did it.

They then (g) arrest the suspect, taking them to a police station and keeping them there. They need to (h) charge the suspect, making an official statement that says the suspect committed the crime.

EXERCISE 2   Read the stories. Which title goes with each paragraph?

A) On Wednesday night a police officer arrested a woman for stealing three chips – his chips! The scene of the crime was a pizza restaurant in Washington DC. The suspect turned up at the restaurant and sat down next to the police officer. She began talking to him and then took one of his chips. What did he do? He asked her to stop, but she took another chip. The officer explained to the woman that this was theft but she didn't pay any attention and took a third chip. The officer arrested her, took her to the police station, and charged her with the theft of 'French-fried potato … quantity: three'. After eating the chips, there wasn't any evidence. But the witness report was probably sufficient!

B) A human arrow helped the police to arrest two suspects in Surrey last Friday. Two men broke into an old building, and a witness called the police. The police immediately sent a helicopter to investigate and look for the men. A group of children and adults saw the police helicopter overhead and also two suspicious men running across a field. They realised the helicopter was in search of the two men, so they came up with an idea. They quickly got on the ground and formed an arrow to guide the helicopter to the suspects. The police caught the two men and charged them with suspected burglary. Surrey police are still looking into the crime but they thanked the children and adults for their fast reactions.

C) A 91-year-old woman destroyed a work of art in a museum in Nuremberg, Germany, last week. The work of art cost almost $90,000. So, how did this happen? The woman came across a piece of paper at the museum with an old crossword on it. She decided to try to do the crossword, using a pen (but without looking up the answers in a dictionary!). Later she found out that the crossword was in fact a work of art called Reading Work Piece by the artist Arthur Koepcke. Next to the work of art, the artist wrote a sign that said 'Insert words'. When the police questioned the old lady, she said she simply followed the artist's instructions. They worked out that it was probably just a misunderstanding and that the interactive art in the museum possibly confused her!

EXERCISE 3   Read the stories again and answer the questions

1  Where and when did a woman steal a police officer's chips?

In a pizza restaurant in Washington DC, on Wednesday night.

2  What happened each time the woman took one of the officer's chips?

First, he asked her to stop; then he explained it was theft; the third time, he arrested her.

3  Why did a group of children and adults form a human arrow?

To guide the police helicopter to the two suspects.

4  How did the story of the human arrow end for the criminals, the police and the children and adults?

The police caught the criminals and they thanked the children and adults for their help.

5  What do we know about the work of art that the old lady destroyed?

It cost almost $90,000 and was by the artist Arthur Koepcke.

6  Why did the elderly woman say she wrote on the work of art?

She said she was simply following the artist's instructions.

7  Why do the police think the elderly woman wrote on the crossword?

They think the interactive artwork (a sign saying 'Insert words') confused her.

EXERCISE 4   What do the underlined words and phrases mean?

Guess the meaning of these words and phrases from the stories, then check in your dictionary.

 

 

pay any attention – listen or watch someone or something carefully

sufficient – enough

got on the ground – lie or crouch down

in fact – used to say that something is true, even if it's surprising

Insert – to put or fit something into something else

misunderstanding – not understanding something correctly

EXERCISE 5  In your opinion, are the people in the stories criminals? What makes you say that? Use ideas from the text and other information to justify your opinion. Then share your ideas.

 

Gateway B1 - Unit 2  |  Section 2

Example: I would say that the woman in Story A is a criminal, but she's not a criminal like an arsonist or a murderer. Nobody was hurt, the restaurant didn't lose money, and the officer only lost three chips! I believe the police should investigate more important crimes than the theft of three chips. If a normal person lost three chips, the police probably wouldn't do anything.
